tickets.title: F-9b (1/2): preflight does not check that a MAPPED ACCOUNT exists, so a typo silently removes protection
tickets.defect:
`RunPreflight` validates that a mapped account's FIRM exists in `FirmProfiles` (`P2-8`) and that a profile's enabled sub-rule has a non-zero amount. It never checks the ACCOUNT NAME.

`AccountFirmMap` is keyed by account name and nothing compares it to the platform. Five entries went live on 2026-08-13 and the box reports 96 accounts; the operator's own spelling of `Sim_All_Day_ORB` in that session used a HYPHEN. The failure is SILENT: `ResolveEffectiveFirmConfig` falls back to the top-level `TrailingDD`/`DailyLoss` block, which on this box is deliberately `Enabled: false`, so the account gets NO firm rule and the config still reads as mapped.

This is `P1-90`'s class one layer out. There, a name that did not resolve placed an order on an arbitrary account; here it removes protection from the right one.
tickets.spec:
In `RunPreflight`, extend the existing `(f) FirmMirror validation` block. Keep every check already there, and add exactly ONE new check.

**THE ACCOUNT-EXISTS CHECK.** For every entry in `AccountFirmMap` with a non-empty firm name, the account must be present in `Account.All` by name, compared `OrdinalIgnoreCase` -- matching how `ResolveEffectiveFirmConfig` looks it up, because otherwise preflight would pass a mapping the evaluator cannot use, or refuse one it can.

On failure call `result.Fail("FIRM_MIRROR", ...)` and `break`, matching the two loops already in that block. The message MUST name the unresolvable account name, and MUST say how many accounts the platform is reporting -- that is `P1-90`'s shape: a refusal that does not tell you what IS available is not actionable, and a preflight failure means the guard does not arm at all.

⚠️ **The check applies to an account reporting ZERO equity too.** 89 of the 96 accounts on this box read zero -- expired or unconnected prop accounts the connection still lists -- and they still EXIST, so a mapping to one is legitimate and must not be refused for that reason, while a mapping to a name no account has must be refused even though such an account could never be measured. A test asserts exactly this pair.

⚠️ **A SIZE check is NOT part of this ticket.** `FirmProfile.AccountSize` exists and two of the five red assertions are about it; `T2` does that. Leave them failing -- they are not in this ticket's `expect_green` and you cannot make them pass without writing the other check.

Change nothing else: not the `P2-8` firm-name check, not the `Amount <= 0` check, not any other preflight clause. Do not make `RunPreflight` read anything besides `_config` and `Account.All`.
tickets.context:
The block you are extending is `(f)` in `RunPreflight`, guarded by `if (_config.FirmMirror != null && _config.FirmMirror.Enabled)`. It already contains two loops, each ending in `result.Fail("FIRM_MIRROR", ...)` then `break`. Match that shape.

`Account.All` is a static list. In the test build it is a settable stub, which is how the tests place and remove accounts; in the real NT8 build it is the platform's. `Account.Get(AccountItem.CashValue, Currency.UsDollar)` is how equity is read elsewhere in this file -- see `GetAccountSnapshots`, which computes `CashValue + UnrealizedProfitLoss` and is the expression to match.

`FirmProfile.AccountSize` was added by hand in the commit that added these tests, with the reasoning on it: 0 means unstated, and the field exists so that a dollar limit is derived from the account rather than guessed (`CONFIG_DEFAULTS` R3).

Why preflight and not the evaluator: `ResolveEffectiveFirmConfig` is documented as NOT depending on preflight having run, because config can be reloaded while armed -- so it must keep falling back silently rather than throwing. Preflight is the place that can refuse. ⚠️ And note the cost of that choice, which is why every message must name its offending value: a preflight failure means the guard does NOT arm, so a false refusal removes all protection. `SaveAndReloadConfig` does not re-run preflight, so a bad mapping posted while armed will not be caught until the next restart -- at which point the box comes up disarmed with nothing about the config file looking wrong.
expect_green: a mapping to a non-existent account refuses to arm
the refusal names the account that does not resolve
a mapping to an account the platform does not report still refuses

regions.note: The whole method. Only the `(f) FirmMirror validation` block changes; every other clause -- the account-count check, the mode check, StopGuard.OnMissing, the MinShadowSessions soft gate, the override friction minimum, and both existing firm checks -- must come back byte-identical. Several of them are the only thing standing between a misconfiguration and an armed guard, and each has its own defect ID.

tickets.title: F-9b (2/2): nothing checks that the account behind a plan named -100K is a 100k account
tickets.defect:
`FirmProfiles` is keyed by PLAN (`Apex-100K`, `TakeProfitTrader-50K`) precisely because one dollar amount cannot serve a 50k and a 100k, and this box holds both. `FirmProfile.AccountSize` records the size the amounts were derived for and **nothing reads it** -- which makes it exactly the dead field this codebase keeps filing (`P1-77`, `P2-25`, `P2-78`).

Mapping a 50k account to a 100k plan puts the guard's floor BELOW the firm's own threshold, so the firm fails you before the guard speaks. That is `CONFIG_DEFAULTS` R3's stated failure mode, in the direction that costs money. And it is not hypothetical: research on 2026-08-13 found that BOTH plans deployed by `F-9` carry the wrong amounts for the size in their key -- the `TakeProfitTrader-50K` profile holds TPT's **25K** max loss and the `Apex-100K` profile holds Apex's **50K** row exactly.
tickets.spec:
In `RunPreflight`'s `(f) FirmMirror validation` block, add ONE check beside the account-exists check `T1` added.

**THE SIZE CHECK.** For every `AccountFirmMap` entry that resolves to a present profile whose `AccountSize > 0`, compare the account's observed equity -- `CashValue + UnrealizedProfitLoss`, the same expression `GetAccountSnapshots` uses -- against `AccountSize`. Fail when the relative difference exceeds **0.40**. `result.Fail("FIRM_MIRROR", ...)` then `break`, like the others.

The message MUST name the PLAN KEY, the plan's `AccountSize`, and the observed equity -- all three. 'Size mismatch' without the numbers is not actionable, and a preflight failure means the guard does not arm.

0.40 is deliberately loose. This is a MAGNITUDE check, not an equality check: its job is to catch a 50k account on a 100k plan, not to track drawdown. A threshold tight enough to fire on a normal week is one that gets switched off (`CONFIG_DEFAULTS` R5), and a green test asserts a 50k account drawn down to 47,700 still arms.

⚠️ **TWO EXEMPTIONS, both pinned by tests that are GREEN NOW and must stay green:**
* `AccountSize <= 0` means the plan states no size. Check nothing. The check is opt-in per plan, or an operator adding a plan is locked out of arming until they have researched a number they may not have.
* An account whose observed equity is `<= 0` cannot be size-checked at all. **89 of the 96 accounts on this box report zero**, so refusing over those would mean the guard never arms here again.
⚠️ The second exemption is for the SIZE check ONLY -- `T1`'s existence check still applies to a zero-equity account, and a green test asserts that. Skipping both for a zero-equity account is a hole big enough to swallow the whole gate.

Change nothing else, including the account-exists check `T1` added.
